fields.title: Glioblastoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Glioblastoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Glioblastoma is one of the most aggressive and common forms of primary brain tumour in adults. It grows quickly and tends to recur, which makes it particularly difficult to treat. In Israel, patients with glioblastoma have access to advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment aimed at extending life and improving its quality.

Diagnosis of glioblastoma

  1. MRI of the brain
    The key method in diagnosing glioblastoma, establishing the position and size of the tumour.
  2. Biopsy
    A biopsy or surgical removal of the tumour for histological analysis, which allows the type of tumour to be determined precisely.
  3. Laboratory tests
    Include blood tests for particular markers and general tests to assess the patient's overall health. These can help detect inflammation and assess kidney and liver function, which matters in planning treatment.
  4. Genetic testing
    Analysis of the tumour's DNA to identify particular mutations that may affect the choice of treatment.

Treatment of glioblastoma

  1. Surgery
    The aim of the operation is to remove as much of the tumour as possible with minimal risk to critical brain functions.
  2. Radiotherapy: used after surgery to destroy remaining cancer cells, often in combination with chemotherapy.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Temozolomide is the standard drug for treating glioblastoma during and after radiotherapy.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    Newer treatments directed at specific molecular targets in the tumour or at activating the immune system against the cancer cells.
  5. Tumour treating fields
    An innovative technology that uses electrical fields to suppress the growth of cancer cells.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Leading specialists in neurosurgery, oncology and radiotherapy work together to develop an individual treatment plan.
  • Advanced treatments
    Patients have access to the latest advances in treating glioblastoma, including the newest drugs and technologies.
  • Individual treatment
    Treatment programmes are developed with the genetic features of the tumour and the patient's general health in mind.
  • Comprehensive support
    Psychological, social and rehabilitation support is provided for patients and their families at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of glioblastoma in Israel combines the high expertise of its medical specialists, access to innovative therapies and close attention to each patient's needs, which helps achieve the best possible results against this difficult disease.

fields.title: Optic chiasm glioma: diagnosis and treatment in Israel
fields.bodyHtml:
An optic chiasm glioma is a tumour that develops in the area of the optic chiasm, where the optic nerves cross. It occurs most often in children and adolescents and can considerably affect sight, leading to its gradual deterioration.

Diagnosis of optic chiasm glioma

  1. Detailed review of the medical history:
    • The doctor gathers information about symptoms such as deteriorating sight, headaches and changes in the visual fields, and reviews the family history.
  2. Visual examination and eye tests:
    • Assessment of visual acuity, visual fields and other visual functions to identify abnormalities.
  3. Ophthalmoscopy:
    • Examination of the fundus to identify changes associated with the tumour.
  4. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    • The main diagnostic method, producing detailed images of the structure of the brain and the visual pathways.
  5. Computed tomography (CT):
    • Used for detailed study of the bony structures and where MRI cannot be used.
  6. Optical coherence tomography (OCT):
    • An examination to assess the state of the optic nerve and retina.
  7. Electrophysiological tests:
    • Include visual evoked potentials and electroretinography to assess the function of the visual pathways and the retina.

Treatment of optic chiasm glioma

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Corticosteroids: used to reduce swelling and inflammation around the tumour.
    • Cytotoxic drugs: used in chemotherapy to shrink the tumour and suppress its growth.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Conventional radiotherapy: aimed at destroying cancer cells with minimal effect on healthy tissue.
    • Proton therapy: a more precise method that minimises damage to the surrounding healthy tissue.
  3. Surgery:
    • Resection of the tumour: carried out where the tumour can be reached and surgery does not present a significant risk to the patient's health.
    • Shunting: where the tumour causes hydrocephalus (a build-up of fluid in the brain), a shunt may be needed to drain the excess fluid.
  4. Hormone therapy:
    • Used where the tumour affects the function of the pituitary gland and causes hormonal disturbance.
  5. Supportive treatment:
    • Includes treatment of symptoms such as pain and nausea, and support for the patient's mental health.

Advantages of treating optic chiasm glioma in Israel

  1. A high level of professionalism:
    • Israeli doctors have deep knowledge and many years of experience in treating gliomas and other brain tumours.
  2. Modern equipment:
    • Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach:
    • Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments:
    • The use of the most modern methods and medicines, including proton therapy and the newest cytotoxic drugs.
  5. Comprehensive support:
    • Covers not only treatment of the underlying condition but also support for the patient's mental and physical wellbeing during treatment and recovery.

Treatment of optic chiasm glioma in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves their quality of life.

fields.title: Optic nerve glioma
fields.bodyHtml:
Optic nerve glioma: advanced treatment in Israel

An optic nerve glioma is a rare tumour arising from the cells surrounding the optic nerve, which connects the eye to the brain. This kind of tumour can affect sight. Depending on how far it has spread, it calls for an individual approach to treatment. In Israel, patients with optic nerve glioma are offered modern methods of diagnosis and treatment aimed at preserving sight and controlling the growth of the tumour.

Diagnosis of optic nerve glioma

  1. MRI of the brain
    The main diagnostic method. It allows the tumour to be seen and its size and effect on the surrounding tissue assessed.
  2. Ophthalmological examination
    Includes testing of sight, examination of the fundus and assessment of the visual fields to determine the tumour's effect on vision.
  3. Biopsy
    In some cases a tissue sample may be needed to determine the type of cells precisely and how aggressive the tumour is.
  4. Genetic testing
    May be recommended to identify genetic mutations associated with the tumour.

Treatment of optic nerve glioma

  1. Observation
    Where the tumour is slow-growing, causes no symptoms and does not threaten sight, active observation with regular MRI scans and eye examinations may be recommended.
  2. Surgery
    An operation is considered to reduce the size of the tumour or relieve pressure on the optic nerve, where this is safe and appropriate.
  3. Radiotherapy
    Used to control the growth of the tumour, particularly where it cannot be removed surgically. Israel uses precise methods of radiotherapy that minimise the effect on healthy tissue.
  4. Chemotherapy
    May be prescribed to shrink the tumour, particularly in children, to avoid the side effects of radiotherapy.
  5. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    Being studied as potential treatments for particular genetic subtypes of optic nerve glioma.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    A team of oncologists, neurosurgeons, radiologists and ophthalmologists works together to develop an individual treatment plan.
  • Advanced technology
    The use of the newest methods of diagnosis and treatment, including precision radiotherapy and minimally invasive surgical techniques.
  • A patient-centred approach
    A focus on preserving the patient's quality of life as fully as possible, including protecting sight and minimising long-term side effects.
  • Individual treatment programmes
    Treatment is designed around the particular features of each case.

Treatment of optic nerve glioma in Israel offers a comprehensive approach that combines a high level of medical expertise with access to advanced treatments, giving patients the best chance of a good outcome and of keeping their sight.

fields.title: Hiatus hernia
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

A hiatus hernia is a condition in which part of the upper stomach moves through the diaphragm into the chest cavity. It can cause unpleasant symptoms such as heartburn, chest pain and difficulty swallowing. Diagnosing and treating a hiatus hernia calls for specialist care. In this article we look at modern methods of diagnosis and treatment and the advantages of treatment in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosing a hiatus hernia can be difficult, as the symptoms may resemble those of other conditions of the digestive tract. The following methods may be used to reach an accurate diagnosis:

  • Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy: an endoscopic examination that allows the doctor to see the oesophagus and the upper part of the stomach directly and identify the hernia.
  • Barium X-ray: the patient swallows a substance that makes the organs visible on X-ray, which allows the hernia to be identified and its nature assessed.
  • Oesophageal manometry: a test that measures pressure in the oesophagus and identifies problems with its function.

Methods of treatment

Treatment depends on the size of the hernia and the symptoms the patient has. The main treatments include:

  • Lifestyle changes: moderate physical activity, reducing intake of spicy, fatty and acidic foods, and avoiding meals before bed can help ease symptoms.
  • Medicines: acid-suppressing drugs can help control heartburn and reduce the acidity of the stomach contents.
  • Surgery: in some cases, where conservative measures are ineffective, surgery may be needed to restore the organs to their normal position.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is a medical centre of world class providing high-quality medical care. The advantages of treating a hiatus hernia in Israel include:

  • Experienced specialists: medical institutions in Israel work with experienced surgeons and gastroenterologists who specialise in this condition.
  • Modern methods: doctors in Israel use advanced methods of diagnosis and surgery, which helps achieve the best results.
  • An individual approach: treatment in Israel is adapted to each patient's particular circumstances, which produces the best outcome.

Conclusion

A hiatus hernia is a condition that calls for careful diagnosis and effective treatment. Modern diagnostic methods, changes in lifestyle and surgery can help patients cope with the symptoms and improve their quality of life. In Israel patients can receive high-quality, individual treatment thanks to experienced specialists and advanced medical technology.

Managing a hiatus hernia effectively allows patients to return to ordinary life without pain and discomfort. By consulting experienced doctors and using advanced treatments, patients can regain their health and comfort in daily life.
